1800 GOT JUNK Pricing in Chicago: 2026 Breakdown

If you’ve typed “junk removal Chicago” into Google, you’re probably wondering exactly how much 1-800-GOT-JUNK? will charge to haul away that old couch, garage clutter, or renovation debris. The good news? Chicago’s 2026 pricing is transparent, volume‑based, and designed to keep surprises out of the final invoice. In this guide we’ll walk through the pricing tiers, explain what factors affect the cost, and share insider tips so you can get the most bang for your buck.

How 1-800-GOT-JUNK? Calculates Its Fees

Unlike many local haulers that bill by the hour or by the truckload, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? uses a simple volume‑based model. Your quote is based on the amount of space your items occupy in the back of their truck, measured in cubic feet. Here’s why that matters:

  • Fairness: You only pay for the space you actually use, not for empty space or time spent loading.
  • Predictability: The estimate you receive over the phone is usually the amount you’ll pay, unless you add items on the day of service.
  • Speed: The crew works quickly because they know the exact load size they need to fill.

Standard Rate Structure (2026)

In Chicago, the base rates for 2026 are:

  • Up to 5 cubic feet: $140
  • 5–15 cubic feet: $190
  • 15–30 cubic feet: $260
  • 30–45 cubic feet: $340
  • 45+ cubic feet (custom quote): Starts at $440 and scales up depending on volume.

These numbers include labor, transportation, and disposal fees. There are no hidden charges for loading, unloading, or mileage within the Chicago metro area.

Understanding the volume of your junk helps you avoid over‑paying. Here’s a quick cheat sheet to estimate cubic feet for common items:

Imagine you’re moving out of a one‑bedroom unit and need to dispose of a sofa, coffee table, a TV, and a few boxes. That’s roughly 15 cubic feet total.

  • Base rate (15 ft³): $260
  • Potential add‑on (extra 2 ft³ of paperwork): $0 – no extra charge if within the quoted range

Hidden Fees? What to Watch Out For

One of the reasons many people love 1-800-GOT-JUNK? is the lack of hidden fees, but a few edge cases can affect the final price:

  • Additional Items: If you add items on the day of service that push you into a higher volume bracket, the crew will need to adjust the quote.
  • Hazardous Materials: Items like asbestos, chemicals, or large appliances that require special disposal may incur extra fees. The team will flag these before loading.
  • Access Issues: If a crew must use a ladder, stairs, or a narrow alley that slows loading, a small surcharge (usually $20‑$30) may apply.

These are the only circumstances where the final bill could be higher than the original estimate. The key is clear communication when you schedule the pickup.
